raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been at this for thirty years now, and with the kids grown and off working in town, it's really just me and my husband managing the ten mu. We rotate wheat and maize like most of our neighbors — that's been the system here for as long as I can remember, and I've got no reason to change it.

**Thinking about wheat first**

My wheat usually does around 470-500 kg/mu on a normal year. I went to senior middle school and I've been paying attention to what the extension station says, so I try to be a bit more careful than some of my neighbors who just dump urea without thinking. For my target yield, I plan about 16-18 kg N/mu total, split between base fertilizer at planting and topdressing at jointing. I use a compound fertilizer (diammonium phosphate mostly) at the base to cover my P, and then urea for topdressing. Potassium I don't buy separately — the soil here holds K pretty well and the compound has some in it.

Planting will be around October 10-15, depending on when I can get the maize off. I use Jimai 22 or something similar — improved variety, I buy fresh seed every two or three years from the agro-shop in town. Saving seed isn't worth it on the modern varieties.

For irrigation, wheat needs water at overwintering, jointing, and grain-filling at minimum. Some years I do a fourth before heading if it's dry. The well is metered and electricity costs keep going up, so I don't overwater. Three irrigations is my usual, four if spring is dry.

I'll spray herbicide once in spring for broadleaf weeds, and probably one fungicide at heading to protect against head blight — last year the weather was humid at heading and my neighbor lost some yield to scab, I don't want that.

**Then maize**

After wheat harvest in early June, the turnaround is tight — maybe 3-5 days. I no-till plant the maize directly using a contracted planter (I don't own one, costs about 25 yuan/mu for the service). Plant around June 15-18. I use Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid — these are standard here, good ears, stands up to wind reasonably.

Maize here I fertilize less heavily than wheat because the summer rains give the soil a boost. About 14-16 kg N/mu total, mostly as a compound at planting and one topdress at big flare stage (V8-ish). Last summer was wet enough I only irrigated once at tasseling; dry summers I irrigate 2-3 times.

Pesticide: I always spray once for corn borer and armyworm around whorl stage. Herbicide depends on weed pressure — usually one pre-emergence application right after planting.

**Labor and cost thinking**

With just the two of us and him sometimes working off-farm, I hire for the wheat harvest (combine contractor, ~50 yuan/mu) and the maize harvest (another contractor). That's the reality of our labor situation — we can't hand-harvest 10 mu anymore. Family labor is for the in-season work: irrigation, spraying, topdressing.

Total out-of-pocket is going to be around 700-800 yuan/mu across the year for both crops, so maybe 7,500-8,000 yuan for the whole farm. That's manageable, but it's why I don't over-apply inputs. I don't have deep pockets to waste on fertilizer that just runs off.
